# NIST CAVP test vectors for FIPS 186-4 DSA key pairs, signature generation
# and signature verification.
#
# Source archive: https://csrc.nist.gov/CSRC/media/Projects/Cryptographic-Algorithm-Validation-Program/documents/dss/186-3dsatestvectors.zip
#   retrieved 2026-09-15, SHA-256 10783936d5f2b00434f7ca393ab52df5700ff2166e97bde0d2fcb288e3aa67c3
#   (the archive tests/vectors/fips186_4_ffc_domain_parameters.txt also comes from)
# Files copied from it, complete:
#   KeyPair.rsp  SHA-256 01cb341c2a9567564dc62bd26784b1eb022122a52a9bc318643f6edae17f4651
#   SigGen.txt   SHA-256 870cf89022274b1a5c7701525f9bf4293fdeb8b19c2719e2158afdbc88a12ee1
#   SigVer.rsp   SHA-256 c7d33d9b5a908e1beb583104c16bfbef63fbbe3eff4ebe59504a4a390a665a8c
#
# KeyPair.rsp (CAVS 11.1) gives, per [mod = L=..., N=...] group, a domain (P,
# Q, G) and ten key pairs X, Y = G^X mod P. SigGen.txt (CAVS 11.2) is the
# SigGen response file with the per-message secret K printed, so each
# signature can be recomputed exactly: per [mod = L=..., N=..., SHA-...]
# group a domain, then fifteen records Msg, X, Y, K, R, S, where R and S sign
# SHA(Msg) under X with nonce K. SigVer.rsp (CAVS 11.0) gives, per group, a
# domain and fifteen records Msg, X, Y, R, S, Result; Result = P means the
# signature (R, S) on SHA(Msg) verifies under Y, Result = F that it does not
# (the parenthesised reason is CAVS's: which of Msg, Y, R or S was changed).
# The SHA-1 groups are included and tested; the crate offers SHA-1 for
# verification of existing signatures.
#
# Records are verbatim; only carriage returns were removed and runs of blank
# lines collapsed to one. Lines starting with # are provenance comments, not
# part of the CAVP files (the CAVP files' own header lines also start with #
# and are kept).
